title: Working from Home May Increase Obesity Risk
paragraphs: Many people enjoy working from home because they do not have to travel to the office. However, a new study from Australia suggests that working from home may increase the risk of obesity.
The study was carried out by Opoku Adabor, an economist at RMIT University in Melbourne, and published in the journal Economic Papers in 2026.

According to the study, each extra hour of working from home per week was linked to an increase in body mass index, or BMI, of about 0.064 to 0.081 points over time. This is equal to about 200 to 250 grams for men and 170 to 210 grams for women. Each extra hour was also linked to a 7.5 to 9.1 percentage point higher chance of becoming obese, which means having a BMI over 30.

Why might this happen? According to the study, people who work from home do less physical activity and eat more meals at home. Adabor explained that people may eat because they are bored, or snack more often because the kitchen is close by. In an office, people usually have a set lunch break. In addition, people who work from home do not walk to the bus or train.

However, Adabor said that the effect could go either way. For example, working from home can make it easier to cook healthy meals and exercise. The problem is that most people do not plan time to exercise.
Adabor suggests that people who work from home should exercise for 30 minutes before starting work, take short breaks to stretch or walk and keep healthy snacks such as fruit and nuts in the kitchen.
According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, about 36% of workers in Australia usually work from home.
